problem: The claim that only a few universities teach this in first-year calculus is misleading. L'Hôpital's rule sits in almost every Indian first-year calculus syllabus; saying otherwise may make a student skip a standard exam topic.

problem: Both use L'Hôpital's rule to find limits that are themselves needed to prove the derivatives used. The derivative d/dx(sin x) = cos x is normally derived from lim(sin h/h) = 1, so using the rule on sin x/x (and on (1−cos x)/x²) is circular reasoning.
